tip: In an 'att' (that) clause 'inte' comes before the verb: 'att han inte hade hunnit'. A main clause would have 'hade inte'.
'Det var kaffe hon ville ha' stresses the fronted word: put it right after 'det var', and the 'som' before 'hon' is often dropped.
'Svara' takes 'på' for the thing answered: 'svarat på mitt mejl'. In Swedish you answer on something.
'Tog skeden i vacker hand' literally means took the spoon in a fair hand: grit your teeth and make the best of a hard situation.
The clause 'som jag förstod det' comes first, so the verb 'var' lands before 'problemet'. The verb stays in the second slot.
'Försäkra' needs 'om' before the clause: 'försäkrade mig om att'. The 'om' is not optional here.
'Velat' is the have-form of 'vilja' (to want), used after 'har': 'har alltid velat' = have always wanted.
'Se efter' is a particle verb meaning look after; the stressed 'efter' shifts 'se' away from plain see: 'han ser efter barnen'.
'Var god och' is a set polite way to say please, literally be good and: 'var god och fyll i formuläret'.
Adding '-s' to a verb usually makes it passive: 'fixas' means gets fixed, with no helper verb needed.
Modal verbs like 'måste' take a plain infinitive with no 'att': 'måste följa', never 'måste att följa'.
Swedish uses 'på' where English says in: 'dagar på ett år' = days in a year.
When a sentence opens with a time phrase, the verb stays second and the subject follows: 'varje söndagskväll lägger jag'.
'Vore' means would be, a polite hypothetical form of 'vara': 'jag vore ytterst tacksam'. Common in formal requests.
Front the object and the verb still stays second, so the subject comes after: 'kaffe dricker jag', not 'kaffe jag dricker'.
'Gå ut och äta' = go out and eat: 'ut' is a verb particle, as in 'ta ut' (take out) and 'se ut' (appear).
'Det var ... som' spotlights one part: 'det var igår som jag träffade henne' stresses when it happened, not what.
Adjective plus 'som' plus subject means as or though: 'trött som jag var' = tired as I was.
'Vända sig till' needs a reflexive matching the subject: 'jag vänder mig till er' = I approach you.
Swedish can move the object to the front for contrast: 'pengar har vi inte, men tid har vi' = money we lack, but time we have.
'Se fram emot' is a fixed three-word phrase for look forward to: 'han ser fram emot semestern'.
'Vore' is the would-be form of 'vara', used for polite hypotheticals: 'jag vore tacksam om ni kunde'.
'Anhåller om' is a very formal way to request, seen in official notices: 'vi anhåller om ert tålamod' = we request your patience.
Use 'tänder' for lights, candles and fire; devices like a TV take 'sätter på' instead: 'han tänder lampan'.
The particle 'ut' turns 'räkna' (count) into 'räkna ut', to work something out or calculate it: 'vi räknar ut svaret'.
'Fylla i' means fill in a form; the particle 'i' is stressed and never drops: 'jag fyller i formuläret'.
Start a sentence with an adverb and the verb stays in second place, so the subject follows it: 'först då förstod jag'.
Dressing verbs take a reflexive, so 'sig' is required: 'ta av sig' = take off your own clothes, as in 'han tar av sig skorna'.
'Tillbaka' (back) works as a verb particle: 'komma tillbaka' = come back, 'ge tillbaka' = give back.
Swedish can place the bare verb first for emphasis: 'sjunga kan hon' = sing, she really can.
